**Yes, you can deploy to production on a Friday afternoon, but it requires approval from the on-call engineering manager.**

The standard deployment window is **Monday through Thursday, 09:00–16:00 Pacific**. Friday deploys are not blocked outright—they just need that extra sign-off [1].

**Key details**
- Every deploy goes to a canary cell first (5% of traffic) and auto-promotes after 20 minutes if error rates and p95 latency stay within 10% of baseline [1].
- Rollbacks are always allowed at any time, without approval [1].
- The on-call engineering manager rotates; you can find the current on-call in PagerDuty or ask in `#eng-oncall`.

**When Friday deploys are *not* allowed**
- During the **holiday freeze** (Dec 18, 2026 – Jan 4, 2027) only standard and emergency changes are permitted [2].
- During the **month-end billing freeze** (last business day of the month until invoices are sent, usually the 2nd), normal changes to the Ledger service are blocked [2].

If you need a Friday deploy, ping the on-call engineering manager for approval before merging to `main`.

**$350 per night** is the maximum hotel allowance for London business travel.

The Northwind Labs travel policy sets hotel limits at:
- **$250/night** in most cities
- **$350/night** in New York, San Francisco, **London**, and Tokyo [1]

You must book through Navan and submit expenses in Ramp within 30 days with an itemized receipt for anything over $25.

**Income eligibility:** Household income under **250% of the federal poverty level** qualifies a patient for the sliding-fee program [1].

**Discount range:** The program reduces visit costs by **40–100%**, depending on where the patient’s income falls within that threshold [1].

**How to start:** Front-desk staff can begin the application at check-in, and no patient is ever denied care because of inability to pay [1].

Emergency access to a customer's workspace lasts **2 hours** and must be approved by **a second engineer** from the support or on-call rotation in Teleport [1].

**Key details:**
- **Duration:** 2 hours (shorter than the standard 8-hour Teleport production session). If more time is needed, you must request again with an update on the case [1].
- **Approval:** A second engineer from the support or on-call rotation must approve the request in Teleport. You cannot approve your own request, and the approver must not be on the same case [1].
- **Prerequisites:** Only allowed when there's an open support case or declared incident that requires it. Every request must reference the case or incident ID [1].
- **Access level:** Read-only by default. Write access (e.g., editing a pipeline) requires the customer's written consent in the case first [1].

**How to request:** Run `nwctl access request --workspace <id> --reason <case-or-incident-id>` [1].

**Halcyon Health** offers more guaranteed annual leave than **Northwind Labs**, especially after year three.

| | Halcyon Health | Northwind Labs |
|---|---|---|
| **Annual leave (years 1–3)** | 20 days/year | Minimum 15 days/year (flexible PTO) |
| **Annual leave (year 4+)** | 25 days/year | Minimum 15 days/year (flexible PTO) |
| **Carry-over** | Up to 56 hours (≈7 days) | Not specified |
| **Paid holidays** | 9 days | Not specified |
| **Sick leave** | 48 hours/year, separate from annual leave | Not specified |
| **Notice required** | Clinicians: 60 days; Non-clinical: 2 weeks | Not specified |

**Key differences**

- **Halcyon** uses a structured accrual system (6.15 hrs/pay period → 20 days; 7.7 hrs/pay period → 25 days from year 4) with a defined carry-over limit (56 hrs) and 9 fixed paid holidays [3].
- **Northwind** describes “flexible PTO with a minimum of 15 days per year that we actually expect you to take” but doesn’t publish accrual rates, carry-over rules, or a holiday schedule [2].
- Halcyon also provides a separate sick-leave bank (48 hrs/year) [1], while Northwind’s document doesn’t mention sick leave.

In short, Halcyon’s policy guarantees more days off (20–25 vs. a 15-day floor), adds 9 company holidays, and includes a separate sick-leave allowance.

**Halcyon Health requires four things before any vendor can receive or handle patient data (PHI):**

1. **A signed Business Associate Agreement (BAA)** — this is the HIPAA equivalent of a DPA. No PHI may be shared, even for a pilot or test file, until the BAA is fully executed [1].

2. **A completed security risk assessment** — the vendor must pass Halcyon’s security review (sometimes “with conditions”) before data flows [1][4][6].

3. **An entry in the Clinical and Business Systems Inventory** — the system/vendor must be listed on the approved inventory maintained by the HIPAA Security Officer [2][5].

4. **For clinical-use tools, a clinical safety review by the CMIO** — required when the vendor’s service touches clinical workflows (e.g., an AI scribe) [2].

**In practice:** The BAA and security assessment are the hard gates; the inventory entry and CMIO review follow for systems that will hold or process PHI in production.

**Yes, Northwind has an analogous “break-the-glass” mechanism, but it’s built for technical support rather than clinical care.**  

| Aspect | Halcyon Health – Break-the-glass EHR access | Northwind Labs – Emergency workspace access |
|--------|---------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------|
| **Purpose** | Open a patient’s chart outside your normal treatment relationship when care urgently requires it. | Enter a customer’s workspace to fix an urgent technical issue (pipeline down, connector broken, customer locked out). |
| **Who can use it** | All workforce members with Meridian EHR access (clinicians, covering providers, telehealth staff). | Support engineers, solutions engineers, on-call engineers. |
| **Trigger** | Unscheduled urgent patient, covering a colleague, telehealth escalation where the assigned clinician is unavailable. | An open support case **or** a declared incident that requires workspace access. “Curiosity” or “it would be faster” are explicitly not valid reasons. |
| **How to invoke** | In Meridian: click **Emergency access** → pick a reason (*Emergency care*, *Coverage*, *Other*) → type a short justification. | Run `nwctl access request --workspace <id> --reason <case-or-incident-id>`. |
| **Real-time approval** | **None** – patient care comes first; access is granted immediately. | **Mandatory** – a second engineer (from support/on-call, not on the same case) must approve in Teleport. You cannot approve your own request. |
| **Access level** | Full chart access for the patient in question. | **Read-only by default**. Write access (e.g., editing a pipeline) requires the customer’s written consent in the case first. |
| **Duration** | Until end of shift, max **12 hours**. Must re-break the glass if needed longer. | **2 hours** (deliberately shorter than the standard 8-hour Teleport session). Can re-request with a case update. |
| **Audit & review** | Every event logged; Privacy Officer’s team reviews within **2 business days**. Unclear reasons trigger manager confirmation. Inappropriate use = privacy incident (sanctions up to termination). | All sessions recorded. Quarterly access reviews by team leads; unconfirmed access is auto-revoked. Access revoked within 1 hour of departure. |
| **Governance owner** | Privacy Officer (Margaret Holloway) – HIPAA privacy policy. | Security team – Information Security Policy (Head of Security approves exceptions). |
| **Underlying principle** | “Minimum necessary” still applies; never for family, coworkers, VIPs, or self. | Access to customer data requires a ticket linked to a case/incident; standing access to production databases is prohibited for everyone. |

**In short:**  
- **Halcyon’s** is a *clinical safety valve* – no gatekeeper in the moment, heavy post-hoc privacy review.  
- **Northwind’s** is a *technical incident tool* – a mandatory two-person gate, short time-box, read-only default, and continuous session recording.

**No — at both organizations, putting sensitive data in Slack is explicitly prohibited.**

**Northwind Labs**  
- The Information Security Policy classifies customer event payloads, credentials, and encryption keys as **Restricted** data, which must *“never leaves production; never in tickets or Slack.”* [1]  
- The Emergency Access guide reinforces this: *“Restricted data never leaves production, so do not paste payloads into tickets, Slack, or a support reply.”* [4]

**Halcyon Health**  
- The Clinical & Business Systems Inventory lists Slack under **“Systems that must not hold PHI”** with the note **“Never, including DMs.”** [2]  
- The HIPAA Privacy & PHI Handling Policy states: *“Never put PHI in email subject lines, Slack, personal notes apps, or AI tools that are not on the approved list.”* [3]

**Bottom line:**  
- **Northwind:** No Restricted data (customer payloads, credentials, keys) in Slack.  
- **Halcyon:** No PHI in Slack, not even in direct messages.  

Use the approved, secure channels each organization provides (e.g., encrypted email with `[secure]` subject at Halcyon; production systems and secure ticketing at Northwind).
cited_titles: HIPAA privacy and PHI handling policy

Based on the production change approval policy and the customer data retention standard, changing the lifecycle rule that deletes archived customer events in Driftwood is classified as a **normal change** because it alters "data retention settings, lifecycle rules, or anything that deletes customer data on a schedule" [2].

**Required sign-off:**

1. **Change approver of the team that owns the affected service** — the team that owns Driftwood (the archive storage service). The engineering team directory or service catalog lists the specific owner [2].

2. **Additionally, if Driftwood is marked as a Restricted service** in the service catalog, you also need sign-off from the **Head of Security** (Tomasz Wierzbicki) or the security on-call delegate [2].

**Other requirements for this change:**
- An **ADR (Architecture Decision Record)** must be created and linked from the PR, per the engineering handbook [2].
- If you are **shortening** the retention period, the account team must give **30-day customer notice** for any Enterprise contracts that reference a retention period [2].
- The PR must carry the `change:normal` label with risk and rollback sections filled in, and approvals are valid for 7 days [2].

In short: start by identifying the Driftwood service owner in the service catalog—that person (or their delegate) is the primary sign-off you need.

Changing the timing of medication reminder texts is considered a **significant change** to a patient-facing clinical system, so it requires a three-step approval chain:

1. **System steward approval** – The medication reminder scheduler (Pillbox) is owned by **Digital Health Engineering — Patient Engagement (DHE-PE)**, whose steward is **Felix Brandt** [2][4].
2. **Clinical safety sign-off** – The CMIO, **Dr. Anjali Rao** (or her delegate, Associate CMIO **Dr. Benedict Osei**) must sign off on the change [2].
3. **CSCAB review** – The weekly Clinical Systems Change Advisory Board (Wednesdays at 14:00 Eastern) must review and approve the change [2].

**Why this level of review?**  
Halcyon treats patient-facing automation (like medication reminders) as a clinical system. The policy explicitly lists “patient-facing automation (reminders, outreach messages, the patient app’s clinical content)” as a trigger for the significant-change process [2]. A past incident (IR-0412) where a scheduler cutover caused duplicate reminders reinforced that any change to the reminder scheduler needs a written runbook and clinical safety sign-off [1].

**In short:** You’ll need Felix Brandt’s sign-off, a clinical safety review by Dr. Rao or Dr. Osei, and a slot on the Wednesday CSCAB agenda.

The three big bets picked at the Cycle 5 pitch review were:

1. **Tributary** — streaming joins (the Enrich step). Scope for the cycle: CDC-backed snapshots, editor preview, dead-letter routing for unmatched events, and a private beta with design partners in October. GA target remains January 2027 [1].

2. **Lantern** — self-serve billing portal so customers can view invoices, change plans, update payment methods, and download usage reports without contacting support. Target: beta in December, GA January 2027 (dependent on payment-provider migration finishing first) [1].

3. **Hydrant** — automatic scaling for ingest gateways per cell, eliminating manual `nwctl scale ingest` runs. Includes the gateway TLS session ticket change from INC-2291 as a small batch item [1].

These were selected from seven pitches during the review held on September 8, 2026 (moved from Monday for Labor Day) [1].

**365 days** is the current default retention period for customers' archived event data.

This is set in the **Customer data retention standard v2** (effective September 15, 2026), which reduced the default archive retention from 400 days to **365 days** and renamed the cold store to **Driftwood** [2]. The standard specifies:

| Data | Where it lives | Default retention |
|------|----------------|-------------------|
| Archived event payloads | Driftwood | **365 days** |

Enterprise customers can contract for longer retention (up to 730 days) with security-team approval, but the default for all customers is 365 days [2].
